claim.summary: Partition killer degree: on the functional pigeonhole system (Booleanity, hole and functionality axioms, pigeon axioms Q_i = 1 - sum_h x_ih, multilinear ring) with at least two pigeons, two distinct ones written 1 and 2, N holes and D <= ceil(N/2), for the partition error E_A = sum_{j in A} x_1j + sum_{j not in A} x_2j with 1 <= |A| <= N - 1 and D >= 2, the least degree K <= D - 1 of a surviving killer (u in V_K outside the degree-D closure C with u E_A in C) is: (a) 1 in characteristic 2, killer sum_{j in A}(x_1j + x_2j), E_A + Q_2 being idempotent modulo the hole and functionality closure H; (b) 1 in every characteristic when A = {j} (killer x_2j) or A's complement is {h} (killer x_1h); (c) in characteristic other than 2, with 2 <= |A| <= N - 2 and N - |A| >= 3 or |A| >= 3, no linear killer survives (cor:partition-transfer-every-k at K = 1 and an evaluation on partial matchings); (d) in characteristic other than 2, with 2 <= |A| <= N - 2 and D >= 3, it is 2, killer the monomial x_1h x_2j, h not in A, j in A, which kills in every field; (e) in characteristic other than 2, from D >= 3, two partition errors E_A, E_B with A and B meeting and not covering the holes, one of them of size between 2 and N - 2, have least common surviving killer degree 2, by x_1h x_2j with j in A cap B, h outside A cup B.

claim.summary: Partition transfer at every K: on the functional pigeonhole system over any field, with two distinct pigeons 1, 2 among any number, N holes, D <= ceil(N/2), 1 <= K <= D - 1 and rho = max(2K - 1, K + 2): if N - |A| >= rho, Ann_C(E_A) cap V_K = Ann_H(E_A + Q_2) cap V_K + C cap V_K, and if |A| >= rho the same with E_A + Q_1, so the single excess of E_A is 0; for partition errors E_{A_1}..E_{A_r} with representatives R_i = E_{A_i} + Q_2 or + Q_1 (edges in L_i = A_i or its complement) and N - |L_1 cup ... cup L_r| >= rho, the common kernel modulo C is the intersection of the Ann_H(R_i) cap V_K plus C cap V_K, so dim J = a, a the largest over choices of one representative per error of their domain common kernel plus C cap V_K. At the top degree D = ceil(N/2) = K + 1 with N <= 8, every E_A with |A| <= floor(N/2) - 1 or |A| >= ceil(N/2) + 1 has single excess 0. Proof: E_A - (E_A + Q_2) is a pigeon axiom, and lem:low-hole-linear-transfer with P = {1, 2}.

claim.summary: Over a commutative coefficient ring, let C be a degree-D pseudoideal and w_1..w_r polynomials. If s has degree <=sigma, s w_i - w_i lies in C for every i and s p lies in C, then f=1-s kills every w_i and f p - p lies in C, so f preserves p modulo C; a sufficient case is s = sum_i a_i w_i with w_i p in C and deg a_i + deg w_i + deg p <= D, and then s^2 = s modulo C when deg a_i + sigma + deg w_i <= D. Over a field, if C is the degree-D part of the vanishing ideal of a finite X and k <= min(D - max deg w_i, D - deg p), a polynomial f of degree <=k kills every w_i with fp outside C exactly when f vanishes on the union Z of the w_i's supports on X and not at every point of supp(p) minus Z; the first such degree is an interpolation degree on X. On the cube 1-s is the reduced product of denominators; for pigeonhole hole factors it is the empty-column indicator.
claim.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer; the general form, the (a)-(b) gap and the comparison with the reduced product are its corrections.

claim.summary: Parity product repair: over any field of characteristic other than 2, on the cube {0,1}^n with the Boolean axioms and J the degree-D part of their closure, take 1 <= l <= n lines with protected class 1 and errors E_t = -2 x_t, and the product line with combined error E_c = prod_{t<=l}(1-2x_t) - 1. (a) If D >= l+1, every common repair of E_1..E_l (f of degree K with soundness on the window D-K, E_t f in J, f not in J) has degree >= l, attained by prod(1-x_t). (b) If D >= l + ceil(l/2), a repair of E_c has degree >= ceil(l/2), attained by prod_{i<=floor(l/2)}(1-x_{2i-1}-x_{2i}) times (1-x_l) for odd l. The lower bounds hold at every D. (c) On the pigeonhole matching domain Y (m >= l pigeons, h >= l holes, h >= l+1 for odd l for the upper bound; J the degree-D part of the closure of the Boolean, hole and functionality axioms) with diagonal errors E_t = -2 x_tt and D >= l + ceil(l/2), both the common repair and the combined-error repair have least degree ceil(l/2): upper bound prod x_{2i-1,2i} (times x_{l,l+1} for odd l), lower bound by Moebius extraction of a coefficient's non-diagonal edges B, which leaves a nonzero function of degree <= deg f - |B| on a diagonal cube of >= l - 2|B| coordinates vanishing on odd parity. The saving on the cube is in the repair's degree K only: the combined reading needs D >= l + ceil(l/2) against l + 1. Proof of (a), (b): J is the cube's vanishing ideal within degree; E_c is nonzero exactly on odd x_1+..+x_l; in the basis y = 1-2x a function vanishing there satisfies f = f y_1..y_l, so its coefficients are symmetric under complementing [l].
claim.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with corrections and a follow-up that checked part (c)'s Moebius extraction; a degree check over F_3 and F_5 for l <= 6 agrees.

formalization.scope: Informal proof or computation; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: For these cancelling errors a product line's combined-error saving holds on the cube but not on the matching domain: on the cube the repair degree is ceil(l/2) against l, at the larger closure degree l + ceil(l/2); on the pigeonhole matching domain with diagonal errors, blocking edges give the common repair the parity bound.

claim.summary: Over any field, for finite nonempty X_nu in disjoint variable blocks and X their product, with degree the least degree of a representing polynomial: the least degree of a nonzero function supported in a product set prod A_nu is sum m_nu (m_nu the least degree of a nonzero function on X_nu supported in A_nu), and degree is additive on products of block functions (union of block Groebner bases, leading monomials multiply). Hence in the degree-D vanishing ideal of X, block-local errors of degree<=e with supports Z_nu have surviving common killers of degree k (k+e<=D) exactly when k>=sum m_nu for A_nu=X_nu minus Z_nu. A separating idempotent s with s w_i = w_i and s vanishing off the union U of supports (a span generator) equals 1_U on X, so 1-s has degree sum delta(1_A_nu), which on cubes can exceed sum m_nu by the factor b (errors at block origins of {0,1}^b: m=1, delta=b); a general idempotent protecting a 0/1-valued least killer p, s=1-p, costs sum m_nu where such a p exists (always over F_2; not over F_3 on {0,1,2}); protecting one point x_0 costs sum m_nu(x_0), the blocks' least degrees of functions supported in A_nu and nonzero at x_0, which can exceed sum m_nu. Degree additivity is the standard tensor fact, proved here for finite product sets.

claim.summary: For finitely many module errors vanishing after localization and a protected element surviving there, a product of denominators kills all errors and preserves the element, with additive filtration cost. Fixed linear common-kernel survival descends across finite field extensions without degree increase. Controls: in k[x,y]/(x,y)^2 no annihilator of (x) preserves y; in k[t]/t^(m+1) annihilators of (t) first occur at degree m; in k[u,v]/(u^2,v^2) useful f=u is nilpotent and localization at it is zero; rank-one error data at t distinct evaluation points still require locator degree at least t.
claim.assessment: Working elementary transfer proofs and exact algebraic counterexamples, passed by the sole medium reviewer. Finite-extension scope retained for the motivating use. Support, matrix rank and scalar extension alone give no universal cheap multiplier theorem.
